title: Chromatic Block-Gibbs p-Bit Decoding of QLDPC Codes
authors: Mert Gökduman, Cyril Guyot, Henry D. Pfister
abstract: We introduce a parallel decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes based on probabilistic bits (p-bits), tunable stochastic binary units controlled by local fields. The idea is that predicted error configurations, interpreted as explanations of the observed syndrome, are updated stochastically using local Gibbs conditionals, while a progressively strengthened parity penalty drives the search toward syndrome-valid configurations. A coloring of the decoding graph enables parallel block updates, and independent replicas and restarts provide trajectory diversity. The best candidate encountered during the search is returned, mirroring the candidate-selection strategy of recent ensemble decoders. At the stated update budgets, the resulting logical error rates are on par with leading decoders under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise. While the total number of variable resamplings can be substantially larger than the message-update count of BP-based alternatives, the numerical results establish constraint-annealed p-bit dynamics as a competitive stochastic alternative for QLDPC decoding and motivate further study of hardware-native implementations.
summary: This work introduces a novel decoding algorithm for QLDPC codes called constraint-annealed p-bit decoding. It uses stochastic sampling and parallel updates to efficiently search for error corrections. The method proves to be a competitive alternative to message-passing decoders for achieving fault tolerance in quantum computing.
main_problem: Developing an efficient and robust decoder for Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes, which are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: The proposed constraint-annealed p-bit decoder achieves logical error rates competitive with leading decoders under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise models.
method: The decoder employs a stochastic search strategy using probabilistic bits (p-bits) and combines this with constraint annealing and parallel updates via graph coloring.
model_or_system: The system involves QLDPC codes defined by a parity-check matrix H, and the decoding process is modeled using tunable stochastic binary units (p-bits) to find error corrections.
key_observables: Logical error rates, block failure rates, and the minimum Hamming weight of the found candidate.
important_parameters: The annealing strength parameter (beta), the number of replicas (R), and the update budget (K).
main_assumptions: The comparison is made at explicitly stated update budgets, and the method relies on the assumption that stochastic sampling can efficiently explore the solution space.
figures_summary: Figures compare block failure rates vs. bit-flip rate (code-capacity noise) and logical error rates vs. physical error rate (circuit noise) against established decoders.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the p-bit framework, details the constraint-annealed Gibbs sampling process, and evaluates its performance against state-of-the-art decoders under various noise models.
why_interesting: The use of stochastic dynamics (p-bits) and annealing techniques to solve a hard constraint satisfaction problem (syndrome decoding) provides an interesting analogy to non-equilibrium statistical physics methods applied to quantum error correction.

The p-bit decoder (linear β : 0.175 →1.75, 256 replicas, up to 3000 sweeps per leg and 24 legs) is compared with BP, BP+OSD-0 [8], BPGD [18], and impulse decoding [24].

Logical error rate per logical qubit per syndrome round versus physical error rate for the [[72, 12, 6]], [[144, 12, 12]], and [[288, 12, 18]] bivariate-bicycle codes under uniform circuit-level noise. The p-bit decoder acts on the DEM obtained by retaining the X-error component, while the correlated p-bit decoder acts on the full undecomposed DEM. Reference curves: Cascade [38], Tesseract [39], Relay-BP [21], impulse decoding [24], and BP+OSD [8].
